svg.title: Page 2 — The Two Brains
svg.desc: Illustrated comparison of Brain 1's auditable deterministic ranking and Brain 2's independent text-only LLM critique, including score calculation, evidence boundaries, and abstention criteria.
svg.text: Two brains, two different views of the case
PAGE 2 · BRAIN 1 BUILDS THE RANKING · BRAIN 2 CAN CHALLENGE IT
WHY USE TWO BRAINS?
Not to average two guesses. The program keeps an auditable evidence-based ranking
separate from a limited, independent LLM opinion.
BRAIN 1 · THE DETERMINISTIC RULE ENGINE
Purpose
Calculate a traceable ranking from explicit evidence.
Brain 1 receives
• Structured interview answers and adaptive follow-up answers
• Numeric measurements extracted from an accepted photo
• Troubleshooting check results already logged on this case
How the scores are built
1. Score each candidate cause independently; each starts at prior 0.15.
2. Add the log-odds contributions of rules that match the case.
3. Scale photo-signal contributions by distance from the normal baseline
when the rule calls for it; do not automatically give full weight at a threshold.
4. Convert each result with sigmoid, sort causes, and retain the evidence trail.
Rule weights are configured engineering evidence; edits affect the live ranking and are marked.
HOW TO READ BRAIN 1'S SCORES
• Each cause has its own score; the scores are not normalized to total 100%.
• They are case-specific rule scores, not calibrated real-world probabilities.
• Rank #1 means “best supported by the current rules,” not “proven root cause.”
The evidence ledger explains which rules supported or argued against each cause.
DIRECT CHECK RESULTS ALSO UPDATE BRAIN 1
CONFIRMS a cause → +3.0 log-odds
RULES OUT a cause → −3.0 log-odds
INCONCLUSIVE → no score change
Apply after rules, then sort the causes again.
A check is an observation or test. It is not automatically a machine change.
BRAIN 2 · THE INDEPENDENT LLM CRITIC
What it reads
The operator's complaint + dispenser class + material family only.
It does not receive structured answers, measured photo signals, image bytes,
or logged check outcomes. It cannot reason about evidence it never sees.
What it returns
An LLM-generated score for each candidate cause, kept separate from Brain 1.
These are model opinions, not calibrated probabilities. They are never added to,
averaged with, or used to directly reorder Brain 1's scores.
A critic pick is clear only if both are true: top score ≥25% AND at least
10 percentage points above the runner-up. Otherwise it abstains.
No clear pick / no LLM = no clear objection, not proof of agreement. Critic result is stored and reused on re-ranking.
NEXT → Page 3: how history, chance testing and disagreement determine T1–T4
